title: Verdant Resort offline VPC staging plan & TF modules audit
content:
Context and objective:

This is a working staging/cutover + Terraform modules audit for the Verdant Resort private deployment. Customer requires an air-gapped VPC on their colo rack with Redwood Private control plane over a peered management VLAN. Primary goal: deliver predictable inference at 1k p50 tokens/sec for their concierge chat workload while keeping single-digit token latency SLO for short prompts. This doc focuses on: inventory, conservative sizing, network/HA assumptions, Terraform module compatibility, cutover steps, and open questions for solutions/SE.

High-level constraints & customer notes (from scoping call 2025-02-04):
- Strictly air-gapped: no outbound internet allowed from the inference nodes. Control plane connector will be via an approved jumpbox managed by Verdant infra.
- Data residency: logs and customer PII cannot leave their private storage (object store).
- Burst to 3x demand during holiday weeks; baseline steady-state lower.
- Existing colo: 4 RU with 2x 40GbE switches, ESXi-based hypervisors, local Ceph cluster for persistent volumes.
- Preference for NVIDIA-similar accelerators but they have mixed SKU availability (A10G and A40 currently).

Assumptions made for this staging plan (callout so product/solutions can correct):
- Model: optimized Llama-2.1-like open checkpoint quantized to int8. KV cache benefits are significant for conversation workloads.
- Target throughput per GPU: ~250 tokens/sec for A10G under expected prompt lengths (median 40 tokens) with batched concurrency of 4. We use this to size counts conservatively.
- HA model: active/active across two failure domains within the same colo. Control plane connector is redundant (two management jumpboxes).
- Storage: persistent model artifacts and KV caches on Ceph RBD (S3-compatible object store for checkpoints).
- Terraform remote state: stored in customer’s Vault-backed MinIO with server-side encryption; CI will push via an admin jump host.

Recommended sizing (conservative baseline + burst capacity):
- Serving nodes: 4x A10G-equipped servers (1 A10G each) for baseline. Rationale: 4 GPUs * 250 tok/s = 1,000 tok/s baseline.
- Buffer for bursts: keep 2 spare servers cold/warm (hot spare), able to join cluster via automated TF/Ansible run within 15 minutes.
- CPU/RAM per node: 24 cores, 256GB RAM to host runtime (LLM cache, batching queues, NGINX/proxy).
- Disk: 1TB NVMe per node for local KV cache and /var/lib redwood runtime storage; 4TB Ceph pool for model artifacts and cold storage.
- Networking: dual-40GbE with LACP, VLAN-separated control/management and inference traffic. MTU 9000 preferred.
- KMS/HSM: integrate with customer HSM for signing and key wrapping (we will use a KMS wrapper module in TF).

Terraform module notes (compatibility/audit findings):
- Modules to use: ri_vpc_peering, ri_bastion_jump, ri_gpu_pool (customized), ri_storage_minio_backend, ri_kms_connector.
- Observations from quick audit of customer's TF repo branch 'verdant/edge':
  - ri_gpu_pool module version pinned to v0.4 with deprecated resource aws_instance. Need to update to v0.8 that uses provider-agnostic host resources (we will vendor a patch for onprem provider mapping).
  - Remote state backend is currently using S3 block w/ legacy ACLs; must migrate to MinIO with server-side encryption and IAM policy restrictions.
  - No existing module for HSM/KMS integration; create ri_kms_connector with documented interface for their HSM operator.
- Action: create a small shim module that maps ri_gpu_pool -> local_compute_resource when onprem flag is set. Keep changes minimal and submitted as PR to terraform-modules repo.

Network & security design highlights:
- Data egress: completely blocked at node level. Only control-plane traffic allowed from management jumpboxes to Redwood control plane IPs via pre-approved proxy.
- ACLs: strict allow-list on management VLAN for only CI/CD IP ranges and Redwood SE jump host.
- Secrets: all runtime secrets stored in customer Vault; Redwood agent will retrieve via flip-key ephemeral tokens issued by Verdant Vault operator (documented in ri_keystore README).
- Bastion: hardened bastion with 2FA and time-limited sessions; terraform module will create ephemeral accounts using Vault's dynamic user creds.

Upgrade & rollback approach (minimizing downtime):
- Rolling model: upgrade model weights by uploading new artifact with new version tag; mark old model healthy until at least 3% of traffic has passed smoke tests.
- Blue/green for runtime binary changes: deploy new runtime to 1 node, run local smoke + perf tests, then roll to remainder. If anomaly detected (latency > 1.5x p50 or token error rate increase), automatic rollback to previous runtime and model version.
- Terraform-driven infra changes are run in plan->apply with automated smoke gating. Use terraform plan outputs validated by the SE (manual sign-off for capacity-upscaling >20%).

Cutover / staging runbook (short checklist):
1) Pre-cutover: confirm model artifacts replicated to Ceph and permissions set, verify MinIO remote state access from CI account, run smoke job against local dev runtime.
2) Network prep: provision VLANs and test LACP failover, confirm MTU 9000 end-to-end.
3) Deploy baseline 4 GPUs via TF apply in dry-run then apply. Verify nodes appear in Redwood Private console and report healthy.
4) Run load test at 50% then 100% baseline, confirm p50 token latency SLOs.
5) Add hot-spare servers and test autoscaling scripts (trigger scripted join/join sequence).
6) Finalize access controls and rotate keys. Cutover weekend window scheduled: Fri 02:00–07:00 local; primary contact: Marco Hsu.

Operational notes / known tradeoffs:
- A10G is a reasonable cost/perf compromise but model quantization profile must be validated. If we run longer-context prompts or use larger checkpoints, recommend migrating 1–2 servers to A40 or A5000.
- KV cache warmup: expect traffic cold-start delay. Consider pre-warming popular prefixes during day 0 cutover to reduce initial latency spikes.
- Air-gapped CI: any Terraform module changes require binary artifacts to be transferred via approved media or via the jumpbox pipeline. This increases patch turnaround time; document expected timelines for security sign-off.

Open questions / items for customer & solutions team (TODOs):
- Confirm whether Verdant will allow a short-lived egress tunnel for Redwood support during initial 30-day onboarding (we prefer a limited-scoped connection vs manual jumpbox ops).
- Confirm exact HSM vendor/firmware and operator schedule so ri_kms_connector can be tested.
- Clarify SLA expectations for auto-scaling time-to-serve when moving from cold to hot spares.
- Is sustained 3x burst required for 12 hours or short spikes? This impacts whether hot spare capacity or pre-warmed autoscaling is the right mechanism.

Immediate action items (owner):
- Lila: open PR to terraform-modules with ri_gpu_pool shim (ETA: 2025-02-18).
- Tom: draft ri_kms_connector spec and share with Verdant sec team (ETA: 2025-02-20).
- Priya: schedule lab run to validate A10G int8 perf on sample L2.1 quantized checkpoint (ETA: 2025-02-25).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Could pre-stage a lightweight redis prefix cache for first 24h to reduce KV cold start pain. Worth prototyping in lab.
- Consider a short-lived admission-controller that rejects model upgrades without baseline perf signatures.

Appendix: quick perf math used here:
- Target: 1,000 tok/s baseline. Estimate per-A10G: 250 tok/s -> 4 GPUs. Add 2 hot spares for 50% headroom during burst.
- Memory/CPU tuned for batching concurrency 4; if customer uses higher concurrency patterns re-evaluate RAM by +64GB per concurrency step.

End of draft. Please add comments inline in Confluence link and ping on Slack #private-deploys for any blockers.
